en: Using an inclined plane like a wooden ramp to load heavy boxes reduces the required lifting force, preventing back muscle strain.
Wearing rubber-soled shoes increases friction with the floor, which prevents you from slipping and falling on wet surfaces.
Lifting heavy objects by bending your knees instead of your back uses your leg muscles to counteract gravity, preventing spinal injuries.
Keep strong magnets away from credit cards and phones, because their magnetic fields can erase magnetic strips and damage internal electronic components.
Never touch electrical switches with wet hands because water conducts electricity, which can send a dangerous, potentially fatal shock through your body.
Wearing sunglasses with UV protection blocks harmful ultraviolet light from the sun, preventing long-term damage to your eyes' sensitive retinas.
Wearing earplugs near loud machinery blocks high-energy sound waves, protecting the delicate hair cells in your inner ear from permanent hearing loss.
Always use a dry cloth or pot holder to hold a hot metal pan because metal rapidly conducts thermal energy and can burn your skin.
Eating carbohydrate-rich foods like rice provides your body with chemical energy, which your cells convert into the kinetic energy needed for daily physical activities.
A bicycle's gear system uses multiple wheels and axles of different sizes to change the pedaling force, making it easier to ride up steep hills.
Applying sand or ash on a slippery, muddy road increases surface friction, giving your shoes better grip to prevent dangerous falls.
Unplugging chargers when not in use stops the continuous flow of electrical energy, saving power and preventing the adapter from overheating and causing a fire.
